{{Quote|He never quite '''forgave''' the Republic for '''ending''' his rather profitable governorship.|Governor Quarg on his father|<ref name="MSW13" />}}
'''Quarg'''<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|208|Drexel}}</ref> was the original leader of the [[ship-dweller]]s after they were stranded on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Drexel/Legends|Drexel]], and father of the later [[Governor/Legends|governor]] [[Quarg|of the same name]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Father and a band of followers '''escaped'''... if tumbling out of warp in a laser-blasted spacecraft and limping into the '''Drexel system''' can properly be '''called''' escape.|Governor Quarg|<ref name="MSW13" />}}
The father of the future [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Quarg]],<ref name="MSW13" /> the man of the same name<ref name="CSWE" /> was the governor of the [[Korteen asteroid belt]] during the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], where he used his authority to cover up space-wrecking. Under his leadership the [[asteroid mine]]rs, really [[scavenger]]s, used [[sonic jammer]]s to disrupt [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and cause them to crash into [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]]. The governor then got a portion of the scavenger's profits from recovering and selling the cargo and scrap. Eventually, however, this drew the attention of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], and Quarg was forced to flee from [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]. His ship was badly damaged, but he and his followers managed to escape to the [[Drexel system/Legends|Drexel system]], where they wrecked on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Drexel/Legends|Drexel]]. These people became the [[ship-dweller]]s, and Quarg became their first governor.<ref name="MSW13" />

Drexel was short on metal, so to gather needed supplies Quarg continued to use a sonic jammer to wreck ships that passed into the system. His [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] warned that this policy was causing attacks from the native [[Sea-dragon]]s, but Quarg did not listen. The technicians revolted, but Quarg put down the uprising. However, rather than kill the mutineers he instead set them adrift, intending for them to perish on Drexel's endless ocean. These technicians survived and became the [[Dragon Lords]], enemies of the ship-dwellers.<ref name="MSW13" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|We'll make this planet '''truly''' ours... something my fool of a '''father''' who brought us here was '''never''' able to do!|Governor Quarg|<ref name="MSW14">[[Star Wars (1977) 14|''Star Wars'' (1977) 14]]</ref>}}
Quarg was a greedy man who abused the power of his office to gain wealth, but ultimately was either not clever enough or not lucky enough to hide his misdeeds from the Jedi Order. Governor Quarg spoke of his father often, but ultimately thought him a fool who was never able to tame the planet Drexel. Quarg considered the most foolish move of his father's life to be his mercy during the technician's rebellion. Quarg's father chose to set the ringleaders of the rebellion adrift rather than killing them, a move Quarg dismissed as "stupid".<ref name="MSW13" /><ref name="MSW14" />

Quarg's father had a superstitious view of the Jedi Knights, both hating and fearing them, and likening them to warrior priests or wizards.<ref name="MSW12">[[Star Wars (1977) 12|''Star Wars'' (1977) 12]]</ref>

==Equipment==
Quarg wore a blue uniform with a red cape and a green helmet, which he passed down to Quarg who wore it when he met [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="MSW13" /><ref name="MSW12" />

==Behind the scenes==
Quarg senior was first mentioned, unidentified, in [[Star Wars (1977) 12|''Star Wars'' (1977) 12]],<ref name="MSW12" /> and was first depicted in a flashback in [[Star Wars (1977) 13|the following issue]].<ref name="MSW13" /> ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' later established that his son, Governor Quarg, was a "man of the same name" as his father, implicitly naming the elder Quarg.<ref name="CSWE" />
